transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-12-05
- Time: 15:00 PST
- Duration: ~52 minutes
- Attendees: Maya (AE), Diego (SE) — Redwood; Noah (Head of ML), Lena (Platform Eng), Marcus (Security), Asha (PM) — Sable Analytics

Summary (auto): Align on sprint-zero tasks, security handoffs, pilot schedule.

[00:00:00] Maya (AE): All right everyone, thank you for joining. This is Maya from Redwood Inference and with me is Diego, our solutions engineer. Quick check, can everyone hear me?
[00:00:08] Noah: Yep, audible on my end.
[00:00:10] Lena: Loud and clear.
[00:00:12] Marcus: Good.
[00:00:13] Maya: Great. Today the goal is a short sprint-zero kickoff — ops and security alignment before we start the 6-week pilot. We want to confirm success criteria, network requirements, and security artifacts. I'll hand off to Diego for a quick ops overview and then Marcus, we'll carve out the security topics.
[00:00:30] Diego (SE): Thanks Maya. Quick context: Redwood offers three deployment modes — hosted API, Dedicated reserved pools, and Private (VPC/on-prem). For pilots we usually start hosted unless there's a hard isolation or residency requirement. For Sable, we heard from Noah that latency and cost are both important, and you have some regulatory constraints. Correct?
[00:00:48] Noah: Correct. We're building real-time summarization for financial reports, p95 latency ideally <200ms for ~80–120 token responses, and we want to cap cost to keep unit economics positive.
[00:01:02] Asha: Also want to ensure we can audit request/response logs for a subset of traffic.
[00:01:07] Diego: Perfect. For latency the knobs are model selection, batching, and KV/prefix cache. We'll propose a default batching policy for the pilot and also a prefix caching configuration for recurring prompts.
[00:01:22] Lena: One question — network. We need VPC peering for the pilot? We have strict egress rules and need to know if Redwood can do VPC peering or if we should use a proxy.
[00:01:33] Maya: We support VPC peering for Private deployments and can provide private endpoints for Dedicated. For hosted, we can do IP allowlists and TLS, but not VPC peering. If you need peering or customer-managed subnet, that's Private.
[00:01:46] Marcus: For security: SOC 2 Type II docs, KMS integration for keys, and audit logs retention policy — those are make-or-break. Also we prefer SSO via Okta SAML and RBAC.
[00:01:58] Maya: Understood. We'll share SOC 2, our compliance pack, and KMS integration notes. Diego, can you outline our KMS/HSM support?
[00:02:06] Diego: Yeah. Redwood supports customer-managed keys via cloud KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) and we have HSM options for Private. For hosted, we can do envelope encryption and audit logs. There's also an option for bring-your-own-key for Dedicated. Caveat: certain on-prem HSM setups need a short engineering sprint.
[00:02:25] Marcus: Good to know. Also, data residency — some of our customers' docs must remain in the EU region. Is regional pinning possible?
[00:02:33] Maya: Yes, we can pin to region for both Hosted and Dedicated, and Private obviously can be in your on-prem cluster in EU. We'll note that in the runbook.
[00:02:41] Noah: For the pilot we'll likely use hosted-to-start but evaluate Dedicated if p95 can't be hit or cost balloons.
[00:02:48] Diego: Sounds reasonable. Typical flow: hosted pilot -> measure p95 and cost per 1k tokens -> if we can't meet targets we propose a Dedicated pool with system-level batching and weight-based routing.
[00:02:59] Asha: How long to spin up Dedicated?
[00:03:01] Diego: Usually 1–2 weeks after contract and capacity allocation. For a quick perf baseline we don't need Dedicated. We can run a baseline perf test against hosted.
[00:03:10] Lena: On the perf test: what do you need from us? Sample prompts, traffic profile, and any long-context cases?
[00:03:18] Diego: Exactly. We need a representative prompt set, typical request rate (RPS), token distribution, and flag any long-context sessions. If you have KV cache patterns or repeated prompts, that's useful — we can tune prefix caching.
[00:03:31] Noah: We'll assemble a 100-prompt pilot set and a 24-hour token distribution histogram. We can get that to you by next Friday 12/12.
[00:03:38] Maya: Great. Marcus, for compliance, can you list top questions now so we can expedite the packet?
[00:03:44] Marcus: Sure — we need: 1) SOC 2 report, 2) details on encryption at rest and in transit, 3) KMS key lifecycle and BYOK options, 4) access controls and RBAC, 5) audit log retention and export. Also need to know where logs are stored and if Redwood supports an S3 export of logs.
[00:04:02] Diego: We can export logs to customer-owned S3 buckets for Dedicated and Private; hosted has log retention and can push via secure export; we'll document the retention windows.
[00:04:14] Marcus: Ok please note that exportability is required for us.
[00:04:18] Maya: Noted. We'll include log export options in the packet.
[00:04:22] Asha: Onboarding ops — what's the typical sequence and roughly how long to get to traffic?
[00:04:26] Diego: Sprint-zero (this call) -> share security docs and network diagrams -> provide sample prompts -> perf baseline run (30–60 min) -> analyze results and tune batching/quantization -> if needed, spin up Dedicated. From sprint-zero to pilot on live traffic: typical 3–6 weeks depending on approvals.
[00:04:44] Noah: Budget question — do you have an estimate sheet for hosted pilot costs vs Dedicated?
[00:04:48] Maya: Yes we'll send a conservative estimate: expected cost per 1k tokens for the models you want plus Dedicated committed pricing scenarios. We'll include a simple model that maps to your expected RPS.
[00:04:58] Lena: Network specifics — for private deployment, what subnet ranges do you need and what ports?
[00:05:03] Diego: We'll send a minimal requirements doc: egress to our management plane, peering setup, ports 443 for REST, optional gRPC ports if you prefer. We'll provide a CIDR suggestion and a sample terraform snippet.
[00:05:18] Marcus: Regarding SSO — we use Okta and require SAML with Just-In-Time provisioning. Is that supported?
[00:05:25] Maya: Yes, SAML Okta SSO is supported and we can do SCIM for user provisioning. We'll include our SAML metadata and an admin setup guide.
[00:05:33] Marcus: Great.
[00:05:35] Asha: Any limitations we should be aware of for long-context or multi-tool flows?
[00:05:39] Diego: Long-context increases memory and latency; we have optimized kernels for longer sequences but it depends on model and quantization. For multi-tool chains we recommend small batches and function-call streaming; Diego: we can demo that in the dev sandbox.
[00:05:54] Noah: Also curious about monitoring — can we get token-level cost dashboards and per-route latency?
[00:05:59] Maya: Yes, Redwood Console provides token-level breakdowns, per-route/model dashboards, and traces. We can enable a trial retention window for pilot.
[00:06:08] Lena: Will you give us access to a staging org?
[00:06:10] Maya: Yes, we'll provision a staging tenant with limited quotas for your pilot.
[00:06:14] Marcus: One more compliance item — do you have an independent pen-test report or security questionnaire template?
[00:06:18] Maya: We have a standard security questionnaire and a pen-test summary; we'll include both in the security packet.
[00:06:24] Asha: Cool. Timeline recap?
[00:06:26] Maya: Action: Maya send security packet + runbook by 12/06. Between 12/06–12/12 Sable sends prompt set and network diagram. Week of 12/15 Diego runs baseline perf with Lena. After perf we meet to review results and make a call on Dedicated. Anyone object?
[00:06:45] Noah: Sounds good.
[00:06:46] Lena: Works for me.
[00:06:48] Marcus: Fine.
[00:06:49] Diego: I can slot a 45 minute perf window on 12/16 AM; will coordinate with Lena.
[00:06:56] Maya: Perfect. Any final questions?
[00:07:00] Noah: Minor — can you share a quick sample dashboard screenshot so product can see how cost is surfaced?
[00:07:06] Maya: Yes I'll attach a screenshot and the console sample link in the follow-up.
[00:07:11] Asha: Thanks everyone.
[00:07:13] Maya: Thank you. We'll follow up with the packet and schedule invites.
